_doc: Explicit per-combo EXPECTED-TIER whitelist for the Commander Spellbook combo-recall bench. STATELESS INVARIANT: for EACH eligible combo (every card has a gold fixture), the engine's CURRENT reconstruction tier MUST equal the expectedTier pinned here. ANY drift fails loudly and per-combo: a REGRESSION (e.g. Green->Amber, Amber->Missed) is a real coverage loss; an IMPROVEMENT (e.g. Missed->Amber) also fails, with the message 'update the pin for <combo>' — a coverage gain is a deliberate, reviewed pin edit, never a silent moving baseline. A combo present in the run but absent here (or vice-versa) also fails (the whitelist is a list of NAMES, not an aggregate count). The aggregate recall numbers in bench-report.json are a DERIVED REPORT (regenerated by `dotnet run -- --write`), NOT the gate; this file is the gate. Seeded from the run on 2026-06-16 (5 Green / 18 Amber / 10 Missed of 33 eligible).

combos.reason: 2026-07-18 precision-fix investigation (Currency B, following Chatterfang x Pitiless Plunderer -> Green): CONFIRMED honest AMBER, not an engine gap -- do not promote. Both cards' ETB ('you may exile another/target ... permanent/creature you control, then return that card') is an OPTIONAL blink (EffectType=optional, CR 117.7), so PortGraph.cs marks the emit:blink port Gated=true; PortCycle.Firable (ADR-0002 §8) floors ANY cycle touching a Gated port to AMBER regardless of edge Reliability -- verified live (engine.Materialize + FindCycles over the two hand-parsed golds): the 2-hop blink<->etb cycle has Firable=false, LimitingReason='gated (rate-limit / intervening-if)'. Independently, each cross-card blink->etb bridge edge is ALSO Reliability=No/Reason=IsSelf (ObjectFilterRelations.Subsumes on the IsSelf axis): a broad 'another permanent you control' / 'target non-Angel creature you control' blink target can never be proven to hit the SPECIFIC other card needed to fire its self-only ETB (object-identity is a player choice, not a type fact) -- the same object-identity floor as guard:self-watch in kiki-jiki-x-restoration-angel.json (interaction-judge PASS, accretion batch 8, 2026-07-17). Both floors are structural, deliberate (ADR-0002 §8; the general Gated-cycle and IsSelf-Subsumes contracts must NOT be loosened per-card) and already regression-pinned: BlinkFlowArmScopeTest.Felidar_guardian_x_restoration_angel_reconstructs_amber_pure_two_card_blink (tests/magic-ast-tests/Tests/Interaction/BlinkFlowArmScopeTest.cs) asserts this exact combo id (1090-2781, pop 48050) reconstructs AMBER. No interaction gold exists for this pair (kiki-jiki-x-restoration-angel.json witnesses the same shape via a different card pairing), so there is no 'gold ahead of engine' mismatch either. Verified oracle text against oracle-cards.json: Felidar Guardian 'When this creature enters, you may exile another target permanent you control, then return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control.'; Restoration Angel 'When this creature enters, you may exile target non-Angel creature you control, then return that card to the battlefield under your control.'

2026-07-18 Amber->Green: closes the gap the Warren Soultrader + Gravecrawler + Blood Artist audit identified (Warren's 'Pay 1 life, Sacrifice another creature' co-cost pair; PayLifeCost's pay:paylife consume had no flow arm bridging a life-gain emit to it, so CoCostsSatisfied floored every such combo to Amber). Fix: a new LifeCostToPay flow arm (PortFlowMatcher.SelectArm/Captures + a dedicated PayLifeFamily projecting pay:paylife with a real Quantity + You Subject, PortGraphEngine.LifeGainFeedsCost) mirrors ManaToPay/ManaBalanced for life, plus a LifeBalanced check (PortCycle.LifeBalanced, its own field so LimitingReason can name it distinctly from mana) requiring net(life) >= 0 per iteration -- CR-grounded, not a stylistic mirror: CR 119.4 makes paying life a real, bounded loss and CR 119.6 ends the game at 0-or-less life, so a net-negative life loop would kill its own caster after finitely many iterations and is not a certifiable infinite combo; 'some life gain exists' alone is NOT sufficient, only a provable net>=0 is. Traced cycle here: Blood Artist's emit:life:gain:controlled -> Warren pay:paylife (now a REAL materialized RulesDefined/Green edge, Reliability=Yes) -> Warren Treasure -> sac Treasure -> mana:any -> Gravecrawler {B} recast -> Gravecrawler sac'd again -> Blood Artist's dies-trigger (closes). LifeBalanced holds because Blood Artist's 'you gain 1 life' exactly offsets Warren's 'Pay 1 life' every iteration (net 0, non-negative). Every hop Reliability=Yes/Tier=Green, mana-balanced (1 any-mana pays {B}). Shares the SAME accepted over-approximation as the pre-existing GREEN gravecrawler-x-ashnods-altar-x-blood-artist precedent (2034-2577-4871 pinned Green) and that gold's own documented note: Gravecrawler's 'as long as you control a Zombie' recast condition is not modeled as a gate (no other Zombie in this 3-card set), a pre-existing, consciously-accepted engine boundary this fix does not touch or worsen. Full bench + Ast.Tests core ring verified green alongside this change.

RE-PIN (2026-07-18, was wrongly 'Amber'): the prior Amber never actually used Night of Souls' Betrayal — the cycle the engine found was 'Gravecrawler::emit:returntobattlefield:self => Pitiless Plunderer::sac:artifact:treasure:controlled', i.e. a recast Gravecrawler (a Zombie creature) satisfying a 'sacrifice a Treasure' cost, which is impossible (Gravecrawler is never an artifact/Treasure). That was the exact false-positive the RecastSatisfies subtype guard in d7a8b2c1 (fix(interaction): prune coarse self-return from subtype-specific sacs) correctly pruned; the prune just happened to also remove this combo's only cycle, unmasking that the pin was never verifying the real combo mechanism. The real loop needs Night of Souls' Betrayal's -1/-1 to kill a freshly-recast Gravecrawler via state-based action (1/0 toughness) so it dies-and-recasts with no sac outlet at all; the engine has no P/T-lethality reasoning hop for that ('modifyPT' is an inert port today) per libs/mast-interaction/docs/aristocrat-recursion-scope.md §1 row 2 / §4 Decision 5, which predicted exactly 'AMBER at best, likely Missed... out of scope' for this combo when the recursion arm was scoped. Honest current tier is Missed; upgrading to Amber/Green needs a real P/T-lethality flow arm, not a pin edit.

2026-07-18 audit (confirmed no-op, correctly Amber): materialized the 3-card graph directly (PortWalk + PortGraphEngine). The engine reconstructs the SAME 2-card 4-hop cycle as the sibling 1385-3000-5670 (Warren x Zulaport x Chatterfang) combo -- Chatterfang's Squirrel token -> Warren's 'Sacrifice another creature' -> Warren's Treasure -> Chatterfang's token-doubling replace -> back to a Squirrel token -- with every hop already Reliability=Yes/Tier=Green (Warren's sac-cost fodder filter declares CardTypes:[creature] directly, so the 2026-07-18 Chatterfang x Pitiless Plunderer Squirrel-subtype fix is a no-op here too). CycleCards confirms Academy Manufactor sits OUTSIDE the reconstructed cycle, exactly like Zulaport in the sibling combo. The sole limiter is the SAME structural gap: CoCostsSatisfied=false ('unfed co-cost') on Warren::pay:paylife -- no flow arm bridges a life-gain emit to a pay-life cost consume (the engine has no life-cost-vs-life-gain balance dimension; Currency C scope, owned elsewhere this round). UNLIKE the Zulaport sibling, though, Academy Manufactor cannot actually supply that missing life-gain even after a LifeCostToPay bridge lands: its oracle text ('If you would create a Clue, Food, or Treasure token, instead create one of each') is a single replacement whose own Replacement field is itself EffectType=composite (3x createToken: Clue/Food/Treasure); PortWalk's `replacement` branch (PortGraph.cs ProjectEffect, the `effectType == "replacement"` case) calls EmitPort on that Replacement field ONCE rather than recursing into composite children (unlike the top-level ability-effects composite recursion), so the whole triple collapses to one coarse, disconnected `emit:composite` port on Academy Manufactor -- the Food token's intrinsic 111.10b life-gain ability (PredefinedTokens.Registry["Food"] = emit:gainlife, which WOULD project if the composite were recursed) is not derivable from this card at all today. So this specific combo carries a SECOND, narrower, currently-non-limiting projection gap (composite-Replacement collapse) layered under the shared life-cost gap -- fixing the shared LifeCostToPay bridge alone will NOT flip this combo to Green the way it might flip the Zulaport sibling; the composite-collapse gap would also need closing first. Not fixed here (out of this audit's scope; flagging for whoever picks up either gap next). Honest, conservative Amber; not forced to Green.

2026-07-18 precision-fix: the sac->death bridge Chatterfang.sac:creature:squirrel:controlled -> Pitiless Plunderer.ltb:creature:to-graveyard:controlled floored to Amber/Unknown because ObjectFilterRelations.TypeGuaranteed could not prove a bare Subtypes:[Squirrel] filter (no CardTypes) guarantees 'creature' — the ontology's SubtypeToCardTypes['Squirrel'] straddles the non-permanent Kindred pool (CR 308.1/308.2, 110.4; Squirrel confirmed on the CR 205.3m creature-type list). ObjectFilterRelations.cs/Subsumes is UNCHANGED — the general straddle ambiguity stays honest everywhere else (the panel-reviewed squirrel-not-subset-of-creature.json contract test still expects Unknown). The fix is scoped to one call site: PortGraph.cs's sacrifice-COST builder now lifts a subtype-only fodder filter to its permanent card type via the new PortLabel.LiftPermanentCardTypeList, on the reasoning that CR 701.21a guarantees sacrifice fodder is always already a permanent (a Kindred instant/sorcery can never be sac'd), so the Kindred-non-permanent branch is structurally impossible in that one position. The sac-death bridge now certifies GREEN (Reliability=Yes), and the full 5-hop cross-card cycle (sac squirrel -> Pitiless dies-trigger -> Treasure emit -> Chatterfang token-doubling intercept -> squirrel regrowth) certifies Green — CoCostsSatisfied/Balanced/Productive all hold (non-mana output makes it productive per PortCycle's own doc). interaction-judge PASS 2026-07-18 (independently re-verified the CR citations, confirmed zero scope leakage via the full 73-combo bench gate, confirmed the contract test is byte-identical). Verified against Commander Spellbook (community-confirmed 2-card infinite: infinite mana/ETB/LTB/death/sac triggers, requires 'an additional Squirrel' in play, which is a board-state precondition outside AST scope, not a card/engine gap).

2026-07-18 precision-fix investigation (Currency B, following Felidar Guardian x Restoration Angel -> confirmed AMBER, 25a93085): CONFIRMED honest AMBER, not an engine gap -- do not promote. Kiki taps to copy Felidar Guardian (Kiki's target filter {creature,!Legendary,Controller:You} Subsumes Felidar's self-type, CopyAdmits); GraftCopyInheritance (PortGraphEngine.cs) grafts Felidar's ports onto the copy under a synthesized copy identity; the copy's own ETB is itself an optional blink that can target Kiki, and CR 400.7 (new object) means Kiki re-enters UNTAPPED when blinked, renewing its {T} -- the blink-to-tap-renewal dual of the inherited-untap arm (copy-inheritance-scope.md Decision 4; Kiki + Corridor Monitor is the GREEN sibling of this shape, 618-4404). THREE independent floors keep this AMBER, verified live by materializing the two hand-parsed golds (two Cycles emitted, both Firable=false, LimitingReason='gated (rate-limit / intervening-if)'): (1) both cross-card blink->etb bridge edges are Reliability=No/Reason=IsSelf (ObjectFilterRelations.Subsumes on the IsSelf axis) -- the same object-identity floor as Felidar+Restoration-Angel and kiki-jiki-x-restoration-angel.json: a broad 'another target permanent you control' blink can never be proven to hit the SPECIFIC card needed to fire its self-only ETB; (2) Felidar's ETB is OPTIONAL ('you may exile...', CR 117.7) so PortGraph.cs marks emit:blink Gated=true, and PortCycle.Firable (ADR-0002 Sec.8) floors ANY cycle touching a Gated port to AMBER regardless of edge Reliability; (3) copy-graft-specific -- the closing blink->tap-self renewal edge is Reliability=Unknown/Reason='inherited untap is optional/conditional' (Decision 3/4, copy-inheritance-scope.md): a grafted closing ability earns GREEN only when unconditional (Corridor Monitor's plain untap -> GREEN, 618-4404); Felidar's inherited blink is optional, so BlinkReachesSource returns Unknown, capping this edge at AMBER too. All three floors are deliberate, general-purpose design (the Gated-cycle, IsSelf-Subsumes, and optional-closing-ability contracts must NOT be loosened per-card) and already regression-pinned: BlinkFlowArmScopeTest.Kiki_x_felidar_guardian_reconstructs_amber_blink_renews_tap (tests/magic-ast-tests/Tests/Interaction/BlinkFlowArmScopeTest.cs) asserts this exact combo id (618-2781, pop 13066) reconstructs AMBER, and interaction-judge already PASSed this exact combo by name: docs/judgments/verdict-2026-06-16-blink.json item 2 ('Kiki-Jiki, Mirror Breaker + Felidar Guardian (bench 618-2781, AMBER) -- copy-inheritance + blink->tap renewal (dual of inherited untap, Decision 4)', verdict PASS). copy-inheritance-scope.md Sec.2's acceptance table predicted this exact target tier (AMBER) before the blink arm even landed. Sacrifice it at the beginning of the next end step.'; Felidar Guardian 'When this creature enters, you may exile another target permanent you control, then return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control.'
